 Almost 14,000 BMW owners told to park outside in fire risk recall
 A wide range of BMW models sold in Australia are being recalled, after a fault which could lead to a vehicle fire was discovered.
 by 
 Jordan Mulach 
 Published 
 November 21, 2026
 Link copied! 
 Copy failed! 
 BMW X3 
 BMW Australia has recalled 13,696 vehicles which share a common fault, and has told owners to keep their cars parked outside and away from structures due to a risk of fire.
 The recall affects examples of the X1, X3, X5 SUVs, the 228i, 325i, 328i, 428i, 520i, 528i sports coupes and sedans, as well as the Z4 convertible, built between 2011 and 2018.
 “An improperly sealed electrical connector on the water pump may become exposed to moisture over time and short circuit,” BMW said in its recall notice . 
 “A short circuit increases the risk of a vehicle fire, smoke or a burning smell whilst driving or when exiting the vehicle.
 BMW X5 “A vehicle fire could increase the risk of injury or death to vehicle occupants, other road users, bystanders and/or damage to property.”
 BMW added that, “as a precaution, vehicles should be parked outdoors away from structures and other vehicles until the recall has been completed”.
 “Once a remedy becomes available, BMW will contact affected owners to schedule an appointment for inspection. If required, repairs will be carried out, free of charge.”
 Owners have been encouraged to keep their details up to date with BMW to ensure they receive information from the carmaker.
 A full list of affected Vehicle Identification Numbers (VINs) can be found here , while BMW Australia’s recall hotline can be contacted on 1800 243 675.
